entries.title: HTTP Error 500.30 - ASP.NET Core app failed to start
entries.signature: HTTP 500.30 ANCM In-Process Start Failure app failed to start kestrel
entries.cause: The ASP.NET Core Module (ANCM) could not start the app in-process. This is usually caused by an exception thrown during application startup (Program.cs / Startup.cs), a missing dependency, or a bad configuration value.
entries.solution:
1. Run the app directly from the command line with `dotnet YourApp.dll` to see the real startup exception.
2. Enable stdout logging in web.config (set stdoutLogEnabled="true") and inspect the log file.
3. Check Program.cs for exceptions thrown before the host runs (e.g. failing DI registrations, bad connection strings).
4. Ensure the correct .NET runtime is installed on the server.

entries.title: HTTP Error 500.31 - Failed to load ASP.NET Core runtime
entries.signature: HTTP 500.31 ANCM Failed to Find Native Dependencies runtime not found
entries.cause: The required .NET runtime version is not installed on the hosting machine, or the app targets a framework version that is missing.
entries.solution:
1. Install the .NET Hosting Bundle that matches your app's target framework on the server.
2. Verify installed runtimes with `dotnet --list-runtimes`.
3. Restart IIS with `net stop was /y` then `net start w3svc`.

entries.title: HTTP Error 500.19 - Internal Server Error (config)
entries.signature: HTTP 500.19 cannot read configuration file web.config aspNetCore module not installed
entries.cause: IIS cannot read the application's configuration (web.config), often because the ASP.NET Core Module is not installed or the web.config is malformed.
entries.solution:
1. Install the ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle on the server.
2. Validate web.config XML for syntax errors.
3. Ensure the AspNetCoreModuleV2 is registered in IIS modules.

entries.title: Unable to resolve service for type while attempting to activate
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Unable to resolve service for type while attempting to activate controller constructor
entries.cause: A constructor requires a service that was never registered in the dependency injection container, so the framework cannot create the controller/class.
entries.solution:
Register the missing service in Program.cs before building the app, for example:
`builder.Services.AddScoped<IMyService, MyService>();`
Match the lifetime (AddSingleton / AddScoped / AddTransient) to how the service is used. For DbContext use `builder.Services.AddDbContext<MyDbContext>(...)`.

entries.title: Cannot consume scoped service from singleton
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Cannot consume scoped service from singleton lifetime mismatch
entries.cause: A singleton service depends on a scoped service. Singletons live for the whole app while scoped services live per-request, so this creates a captive dependency.
entries.solution:
1. Change the consuming service's lifetime to scoped, OR
2. Inject `IServiceScopeFactory` into the singleton and create a scope when you need the scoped service, OR
3. Inject `IServiceProvider` and resolve within a created scope.

entries.title: A possible object cycle was detected (JSON serialization)
entries.signature: JsonException A possible object cycle was detected object reference loop serialize navigation property
entries.cause: System.Text.Json tried to serialize an object graph with circular references (commonly EF Core navigation properties that reference each other).
entries.solution:
1. Configure the JSON options to ignore cycles:
`builder.Services.AddControllers().AddJsonOptions(o => o.JsonSerializerOptions.ReferenceHandler = ReferenceHandler.IgnoreCycles);`
2. Or return DTOs/ViewModels instead of EF entities.
3. Or use `[JsonIgnore]` on the back-reference navigation property.

entries.title: No database provider has been configured for this DbContext
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException No database provider has been configured for this DbContext UseSqlServer OnConfiguring AddDbContext
entries.cause: The DbContext was created without a configured provider. Either AddDbContext wasn't called, or the options weren't passed through the constructor.
entries.solution:
1. Register the context with a provider:
`builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(connectionString));`
2. Ensure your DbContext has a constructor `public AppDbContext(DbContextOptions<AppDbContext> options) : base(options) {}`.
3. If creating manually, override OnConfiguring with `optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(...)`.

entries.title: A network-related or instance-specific error occurred (SQL Server)
entries.signature: SqlException network-related instance-specific error server not found not accessible connection string SQL Server
entries.cause: The app cannot reach the SQL Server instance: wrong server name, the service is stopped, the firewall blocks the port, or TCP/IP is disabled.
entries.solution:
1. Verify the connection string server name (use `(localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB` for LocalDB, `.` or `localhost` for a local instance).
2. Confirm the SQL Server service is running.
3. Enable TCP/IP in SQL Server Configuration Manager and open port 1433.
4. Test connectivity with `sqlcmd -S server -E`.

entries.title: Login failed for user (SQL Server)
entries.signature: SqlException Login failed for user authentication SQL Server integrated security password
entries.cause: Authentication to SQL Server failed: wrong credentials, the login lacks access to the database, or the wrong authentication mode is being used.
entries.solution:
1. Check the username/password in the connection string.
2. For Windows auth use `Integrated Security=true` (or `Trusted_Connection=True`).
3. Grant the login access to the database and a suitable role.
4. Confirm SQL Server allows the chosen authentication mode (Mixed vs Windows).

entries.title: There is already an open DataReader associated with this Connection (MARS)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException open DataReader associated with this Connection MultipleActiveResultSets async await EF Core
entries.cause: Two queries ran on the same DbContext connection at the same time, usually due to a missing await, parallel queries, or lazy loading inside a loop over an active query.
entries.solution:
1. Always await EF Core async calls and never share a DbContext across concurrent operations.
2. Materialize the query with `.ToListAsync()` before iterating and issuing further queries.
3. As a workaround add `MultipleActiveResultSets=True` to the SQL Server connection string.

entries.title: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
entries.signature: NullReferenceException Object reference not set to an instance of an object null
entries.cause: Code dereferenced a variable that is null (e.g. calling a method or property on a null object).
entries.solution:
1. Find the exact line from the stack trace and check which reference is null.
2. Add null checks or use null-conditional operators (`obj?.Property`).
3. Enable nullable reference types (`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`) to catch these at compile time.
4. For model binding, verify the request actually populated the expected object.

entries.title: InvalidOperationException: Unable to track an entity because its primary key is already tracked
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException instance of entity type cannot be tracked another instance same key value already being tracked
entries.cause: Two different entity instances with the same primary key are being tracked by the same DbContext, often from attaching/updating a detached entity that EF already loaded.
entries.solution:
1. Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only queries.
2. Fetch the existing tracked entity and update its values instead of attaching a new instance.
3. Use a fresh, short-lived DbContext per unit of work.
4. Detach the previously tracked entity before attaching the new one.

entries.title: CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present
entries.signature: CORS policy Access-Control-Allow-Origin header blocked cross-origin request UseCors AddCors
entries.cause: The browser blocked a cross-origin request because the server did not return the proper CORS headers, or CORS middleware is missing/misordered.
entries.solution:
1. Register a CORS policy: `builder.Services.AddCors(o => o.AddPolicy("AllowFront", p => p.WithOrigins("https://localhost:3000").AllowAnyHeader().AllowAnyMethod()));`
2. Add `app.UseCors("AllowFront");` BEFORE `UseAuthorization` and after `UseRouting`.
3. Do not combine `AllowAnyOrigin()` with `AllowCredentials()`.

entries.title: InvalidOperationException: Unable to find the required services. UseRouting/UseEndpoints
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Unable to find the required services AddRouting AddControllers middleware order UseRouting UseEndpoints
entries.cause: Required services or middleware are missing or in the wrong order in the request pipeline (e.g. UseRouting after UseEndpoints, or AddControllers not called).
entries.solution:
1. Ensure the correct order: `UseRouting()` -> `UseAuthentication()` -> `UseAuthorization()` -> endpoint mapping.
2. Call the matching `Add*` service registration (e.g. `AddControllers`, `AddRazorPages`).
3. In minimal hosting (.NET 6+) prefer `app.MapControllers()` after `app.UseAuthorization()`.

entries.title: 401 Unauthorized - authentication scheme not configured
entries.signature: 401 Unauthorized No authenticationScheme was specified DefaultChallengeScheme AddAuthentication JWT bearer
entries.cause: The app uses [Authorize] but no authentication scheme/handler is registered, or the token/cookie is missing or invalid.
entries.solution:
1. Register authentication, e.g. JWT:
`builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme).AddJwtBearer(opts => { ... });`
2. Add `app.UseAuthentication();` before `app.UseAuthorization();`.
3. Verify the client sends a valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header (correct issuer, audience, and not expired).

entries.title: Antiforgery token validation failed (400 Bad Request on POST)
entries.signature: antiforgery token could not be decrypted validation failed __RequestVerificationToken 400 form post
entries.cause: An MVC/Razor Pages form POST is missing or has an invalid antiforgery token, or the data protection keys changed (e.g. after a redeploy or in a load-balanced farm).
entries.solution:
1. Include `@Html.AntiForgeryToken()` (Razor Pages adds it automatically inside <form>).
2. For AJAX, send the token in the `RequestVerificationToken` header.
3. Persist Data Protection keys to a shared store (file system / Redis / Azure Blob) so they survive restarts and scale-out.

entries.title: The SSL connection could not be established / dev certificate not trusted
entries.signature: HttpRequestException The SSL connection could not be established dev certificate not trusted dotnet dev-certs https
entries.cause: The ASP.NET Core HTTPS development certificate is missing or not trusted on the machine.
entries.solution:
1. Trust the dev cert: `dotnet dev-certs https --trust`.
2. If problems persist, clean and regenerate: `dotnet dev-certs https --clean` then `dotnet dev-certs https --trust`.
3. For HttpClient-to-HttpClient calls in dev, ensure the target cert is trusted or configure the handler appropriately (never disable validation in production).

entries.title: Address already in use / Failed to bind to address (port in use)
entries.signature: IOException Failed to bind to address address already in use port EADDRINUSE kestrel listen
entries.cause: Another process is already listening on the port Kestrel is trying to bind (often a previous instance of the app that didn't shut down).
entries.solution:
1. Find and stop the process using the port (Windows: `netstat -ano | findstr :5000` then `taskkill /PID <pid> /F`).
2. Change the port in launchSettings.json or `app.Urls`/`--urls`.
3. Ensure prior debug sessions are stopped.

entries.title: InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains no elements (First/Single)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Sequence contains no elements First Single LINQ query empty
entries.cause: `First()`, `Single()`, or `Last()` was called on an empty sequence.
entries.solution:
1. Use `FirstOrDefault()` / `SingleOrDefault()` and handle the null result.
2. Check `.Any()` before calling First/Single.
3. For `Single`, ensure the predicate matches exactly one element (use `SingleOrDefault` to allow zero).

entries.title: The view 'Index' was not found (Razor view discovery)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException The view was not found searched locations Views Shared Razor MVC
entries.cause: MVC could not locate the Razor view file in any of the searched locations, often due to a wrong file name/path, missing Views folder, or returning a view name that doesn't exist.
entries.solution:
1. Confirm the .cshtml file exists under `Views/<Controller>/<Action>.cshtml` or `Views/Shared`.
2. Match the action's returned view name exactly (case-sensitive on Linux).
3. Ensure the view file's Build Action is `Content` and it is published.
4. For Razor Class Libraries, verify the RCL is referenced correctly.

entries.title: Configuration / connection string returns null (appsettings not loaded)
entries.signature: ArgumentNullException connection string null GetConnectionString appsettings configuration not loaded environment
entries.cause: A configuration value (e.g. connection string) is null because the key name is wrong, the appsettings file isn't copied to output, or the environment-specific file isn't being loaded.
entries.solution:
1. Read it via `builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default")` and verify the key matches appsettings.json.
2. Ensure appsettings.json `Copy to Output Directory` is set appropriately (default web SDK already includes it).
3. Check `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` so the right appsettings.{Environment}.json is loaded.
4. Use User Secrets in development for sensitive values.

entries.title: 415 Unsupported Media Type when POSTing JSON to an API
entries.signature: 415 Unsupported Media Type FromBody Content-Type application/json model binding api controller
entries.cause: The request's Content-Type doesn't match what the action expects (commonly missing `Content-Type: application/json` with a `[FromBody]` parameter).
entries.solution:
1. Send the header `Content-Type: application/json` with the JSON body.
2. Ensure the action parameter is `[FromBody]` and the JSON shape matches the model.
3. Confirm `AddControllers()` is registered and the JSON formatter is available.

entries.title: 400 Bad Request - validation errors (ApiController ModelState)
entries.signature: 400 Bad Request validation errors ModelState ApiController automatic model validation required field
entries.cause: With `[ApiController]`, invalid ModelState automatically returns 400 with a ValidationProblemDetails body before your action runs.
entries.solution:
1. Inspect the response body 'errors' object to see which field failed.
2. Fix the request payload to satisfy the data annotations ([Required], [Range], etc.).
3. To customize behavior, configure `ApiBehaviorOptions.InvalidModelStateResponseFactory`.

entries.title: PlatformNotSupportedException / DllNotFoundException when running on Linux/Docker
entries.signature: PlatformNotSupportedException DllNotFoundException libgdiplus System.Drawing Linux Docker native library
entries.cause: Code uses a Windows-only API or a native library that isn't present in the Linux/Docker image (classic example: System.Drawing.Common).
entries.solution:
1. Replace Windows-only libraries with cross-platform alternatives (e.g. ImageSharp / SkiaSharp instead of System.Drawing).
2. Install the missing native package in the Docker image (e.g. `apt-get install -y libgdiplus`).
3. Check the docs of the failing API for platform support.

entries.title: AmbiguousMatchException: The request matched multiple endpoints
entries.signature: AmbiguousMatchException request matched multiple endpoints route template duplicate attribute routing
entries.cause: Two or more actions/endpoints match the same route template, so the router cannot choose one.
entries.solution:
1. Give each action a unique route template or HTTP method.
2. Avoid duplicate `[Route]`/`[HttpGet("...")]` attributes that resolve to the same path.
3. Use route constraints to disambiguate (e.g. `{id:int}`).

entries.title: EF Core migration: pending model changes / no migrations applied
entries.signature: PendingModelChangesWarning database operation expected to affect rows migrations Add-Migration Update-Database table does not exist
entries.cause: The database schema is out of sync with the EF Core model: migrations were not added or not applied to the database.
entries.solution:
1. Add a migration: `dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate`.
2. Apply it: `dotnet ef database update`.
3. In code you can call `db.Database.Migrate()` at startup for dev.
4. Ensure the EF Core tools package is installed (`dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef`).

entries.title: StackOverflowException from infinite recursion / AutoMapper cyclic mapping
entries.signature: StackOverflowException infinite recursion stack overflow property getter setter recursive call
entries.cause: Code recurses without a base case, or a property getter/setter calls itself (common with auto-properties referencing themselves, or recursive object mapping).
entries.solution:
1. Inspect the repeating frames in the stack trace to find the recursion.
2. Add a proper base/exit condition.
3. For self-referencing property bugs, ensure the backing field is used, not the property itself.
4. For mappers, configure max depth / preserve references.

entries.title: NETSDK1045: The current .NET SDK does not support targeting .NET X
entries.signature: NETSDK1045 current .NET SDK does not support targeting newer version install SDK TargetFramework
entries.cause: The project targets a .NET version newer than the installed SDK supports.
entries.solution:
1. Install the matching .NET SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download.
2. Or lower the project's `<TargetFramework>` to a version your SDK supports.
3. Verify with `dotnet --list-sdks`.
4. Pin the SDK with a global.json if needed.

entries.title: CS1061: 'Type' does not contain a definition for 'Member'
entries.signature: CS1061 does not contain a definition for and no accessible extension method missing using namespace
entries.cause: The code references a member/method that doesn't exist on the type, often due to a missing using directive (for extension methods), a typo, or a missing NuGet/package reference.
entries.solution:
1. Check spelling and the actual type of the variable.
2. Add the required `using` namespace for extension methods (e.g. `using System.Linq;` or `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;`).
3. Ensure the NuGet package that provides the member is referenced.

entries.title: Headers are read-only, response has already started
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Headers are read-only response has already started StatusCode cannot be set middleware
entries.cause: Code tried to modify the response status code or headers after the response body had already begun streaming to the client.
entries.solution:
1. Set status codes/headers before writing to the body.
2. In middleware, buffer or check `HttpResponse.HasStarted` before modifying headers.
3. Move exception/short-circuit logic earlier in the pipeline so it runs before the response starts.

entries.title: HTTP Error 500.0 - ANCM In-Process Handler Load Failure
entries.signature: HTTP 500.0 ANCM In-Process Handler Load Failure aspnetcorev2_inprocess.dll
entries.cause: IIS/ANCM could not load the in-process request handler (aspnetcorev2_inprocess.dll), usually due to a mismatched or missing .NET runtime, a corrupt deployment, or a bitness (x86/x64) mismatch between the app pool and the runtime.
entries.solution:
1. Reinstall the .NET Hosting Bundle that matches your target framework, then restart IIS (`net stop was /y` then `net start w3svc`).
2. Confirm the app pool bitness matches the published runtime identifier.
3. Re-publish the app; verify aspnetcorev2_inprocess.dll exists under the app's runtimes folder.
4. Check the Windows Event Viewer (Application log) for the underlying ANCM error.

entries.title: HTTP Error 502.5 - ANCM Out-Of-Process Startup Failure
entries.signature: HTTP 502.5 ANCM Out-Of-Process Startup Failure process failed to start dotnet
entries.cause: When hosting out-of-process, IIS started the dotnet process but it exited or failed to listen, often because of a startup exception or a missing runtime.
entries.solution:
1. Run `dotnet YourApp.dll` directly on the server to surface the real exception.
2. Ensure the correct .NET runtime is installed (`dotnet --list-runtimes`).
3. Enable stdout logging in web.config and inspect the generated log.
4. Verify the `processPath` and `arguments` in web.config point to the published dll.

entries.title: The LINQ expression could not be translated (EF Core)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException The LINQ expression could not be translated either rewrite the query client evaluation
entries.cause: An EF Core query uses a method or expression that has no SQL translation, so it cannot run on the database server. Since EF Core 3.0 implicit client evaluation is disabled and throws instead.
entries.solution:
1. Move untranslatable logic to memory by calling `.ToList()`/`.AsEnumerable()` before the unsupported operation.
2. Replace unsupported .NET methods with translatable equivalents (e.g. use `EF.Functions.Like` instead of custom string logic).
3. Project only what you need with `Select` before the client-side step.
4. Avoid calling instance methods/local functions inside the query.

entries.title: A second operation was started on this context before a previous operation completed
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException A second operation was started on this context DbContext thread safety concurrency async
entries.cause: A single DbContext instance was used concurrently (e.g. missing `await`, parallel tasks sharing one context, or a DbContext registered as Singleton). DbContext is not thread-safe.
entries.solution:
1. `await` every async EF Core call; never fire them in parallel on the same context.
2. Register DbContext with the default Scoped lifetime, not Singleton.
3. For concurrent work use `IDbContextFactory<T>` to create a separate context per operation.
4. Don't share a DbContext across background tasks or `Task.WhenAll` of queries.

entries.title: Cannot access a disposed context instance (ObjectDisposedException DbContext)
entries.signature: ObjectDisposedException Cannot access a disposed context instance DbContext disposed deferred execution
entries.cause: A DbContext was disposed (end of a scope, or a `using` block) but a deferred LINQ query or a captured reference was executed afterwards — common when returning `IQueryable` or using a context inside a fire-and-forget task.
entries.solution:
1. Materialize queries with `ToListAsync()` before the context scope ends; don't return `IQueryable` out of the scope.
2. Don't store a DbContext in a field of a singleton/long-lived object.
3. In background work, create a new scope: `using var scope = serviceProvider.CreateScope();` and resolve the context from it.

entries.title: Unable to create an object of type 'DbContext' (design-time / migrations)
entries.signature: Unable to create an object of type DbContext add-migration design-time IDesignTimeDbContextFactory
entries.cause: The EF Core tools (Add-Migration / dotnet ef) cannot instantiate your DbContext at design time, usually because the constructor needs parameters that aren't available outside the app host.
entries.solution:
1. Ensure the startup project builds and the DbContext is registered via `AddDbContext` in Program.cs.
2. Or implement `IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<TContext>` to construct the context with an explicit connection string.
3. Specify the projects explicitly: `dotnet ef migrations add Init --project Infra --startup-project Web`.

entries.title: SqlException: Timeout expired / connection pool exhausted
entries.signature: SqlException Timeout expired The timeout period elapsed connection pool maximum pool size reached
entries.cause: Connections aren't being returned to the pool (leaked DbContext/connection), or queries run longer than the command timeout, so the pool is exhausted.
entries.solution:
1. Ensure every DbContext/connection is disposed (use DI scopes; don't hold contexts open).
2. Find long-running queries and add indexes or paging.
3. Increase `Command Timeout`/`Max Pool Size` in the connection string only after fixing leaks.
4. Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only queries to reduce overhead.

entries.title: The entity type requires a primary key to be defined
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException The entity type requires a primary key to be defined keyless model
entries.cause: EF Core cannot find a key for an entity included in the model. It expects a property named Id/<Type>Id or an explicit key configuration.
entries.solution:
1. Add an `Id` property or annotate the key with `[Key]`.
2. Configure it in `OnModelCreating`: `modelBuilder.Entity<T>().HasKey(e => e.SomeId);`.
3. For read-only query types (views), mark it keyless: `modelBuilder.Entity<T>().HasNoKey();`.

entries.title: JsonException: The JSON value could not be converted to type
entries.signature: JsonException The JSON value could not be converted System.Text.Json deserialize type mismatch
entries.cause: The incoming JSON shape/type doesn't match the target model — e.g. a string sent where a number/enum is expected, a null for a non-nullable value, or casing/property-name mismatches.
entries.solution:
1. Make the JSON match the model types; check casing.
2. For enums-as-strings add `JsonStringEnumConverter`.
3. Use nullable types for optional fields.
4. Inspect the exact `path` reported in the exception to find the offending property.

entries.title: Static files not served / 404 for wwwroot assets
entries.signature: static files 404 wwwroot css js not loading UseStaticFiles missing
entries.cause: The static files middleware isn't enabled, the asset isn't under wwwroot, or middleware ordering places UseStaticFiles after a terminal middleware.
entries.solution:
1. Add `app.UseStaticFiles();` in Program.cs (before `UseRouting`/endpoints).
2. Put assets under the `wwwroot` folder (the default web root).
3. Verify the file's Build Action and that the path/casing matches (Linux is case-sensitive).
4. For folders outside wwwroot, configure a `PhysicalFileProvider` with `UseStaticFiles(options)`.

entries.title: Synchronous operations are disallowed (AllowSynchronousIO)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Synchronous operations are disallowed Call ReadAsync or set AllowSynchronousIO true
entries.cause: Code performed a synchronous read/write on the request or response stream, which Kestrel disallows by default for scalability.
entries.solution:
1. Use async stream APIs (`ReadAsync`/`WriteAsync`, `StreamReader.ReadToEndAsync`).
2. As a last resort enable sync IO per server: `serverOptions.AllowSynchronousIO = true` (Kestrel) — but prefer fixing the async code.
3. For libraries that buffer synchronously, enable `Request.EnableBuffering()` and read async.

entries.title: 413 Payload Too Large / request body size limit exceeded
entries.signature: BadHttpRequestException Request body too large 413 MaxRequestBodySize multipart upload limit
entries.cause: The uploaded request body exceeds Kestrel's default max body size (~28.6 MB) or IIS's request limits.
entries.solution:
1. Increase the limit for an endpoint with `[RequestSizeLimit(bytes)]` or `[DisableRequestSizeLimit]`.
2. Globally: set `serverOptions.Limits.MaxRequestBodySize` on Kestrel.
3. Behind IIS, also raise `maxAllowedContentLength` in web.config.
4. For form uploads, configure `FormOptions.MultipartBodyLengthLimit`.

entries.title: Failed to determine the https port for redirect
entries.signature: Warning Failed to determine the https port for redirect UseHttpsRedirection
entries.cause: UseHttpsRedirection can't discover the HTTPS port (no HTTPS endpoint configured, or running behind a proxy that terminates TLS), so redirects are skipped.
entries.solution:
1. Configure an HTTPS URL (launchSettings `applicationUrl`, `ASPNETCORE_URLS`, or Kestrel HTTPS endpoint).
2. Set `https_port`/`HttpsRedirectionOptions.HttpsPort` explicitly.
3. Behind a reverse proxy, use `ForwardedHeaders` middleware so the scheme is detected.

entries.title: JWT Bearer 401 - IDX10223 / token validation failed
entries.signature: Bearer error invalid_token IDX10223 SecurityTokenExpiredException audience issuer signature validation jwt
entries.cause: A JWT was rejected during validation — expired token, wrong issuer/audience, clock skew, or a signing key mismatch.
entries.solution:
1. Verify `TokenValidationParameters` (ValidIssuer, ValidAudience, IssuerSigningKey) match the token.
2. Ensure the authority/metadata URL is reachable so signing keys are fetched.
3. Check token expiry and allow small `ClockSkew` if needed.
4. Confirm `app.UseAuthentication()` is before `app.UseAuthorization()`.

entries.title: 403 Forbidden - authorization policy / role requirement not met
entries.signature: 403 Forbidden authorization policy requirement role claim [Authorize] AccessDenied
entries.cause: The user is authenticated but doesn't satisfy the authorization policy/role/claim required by `[Authorize]`.
entries.solution:
1. Confirm the user's claims/roles include what the policy requires.
2. Check policy registration in `AddAuthorization` matches the `[Authorize(Policy=...)]` name.
3. Ensure the authentication handler emits the role/claim types the policy checks (RoleClaimType).
4. Verify `UseAuthentication`/`UseAuthorization` ordering.

entries.title: Cannot resolve scoped service from root provider / BackgroundService DI
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Cannot resolve scoped service from root provider BackgroundService IHostedService DbContext
entries.cause: A scoped service (e.g. DbContext) was resolved from the root provider or injected directly into a singleton like a BackgroundService/IHostedService.
entries.solution:
1. In a BackgroundService inject `IServiceScopeFactory` and create a scope per unit of work: `using var scope = _scopeFactory.CreateScope(); var db = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<MyDbContext>();`.
2. Don't inject scoped services into singletons.
3. For pooled contexts in hosted services use `IDbContextFactory<T>`.

entries.title: IOptions<T> values are null / configuration section not bound
entries.signature: IOptions Value null configuration section not bound Configure appsettings options pattern
entries.cause: The options class wasn't bound to a configuration section, the section name/property names don't match, or appsettings isn't being loaded for the current environment.
entries.solution:
1. Bind in Program.cs: `builder.Services.Configure<MyOptions>(builder.Configuration.GetSection("MySection"));`.
2. Ensure JSON keys exactly match property names.
3. Inject `IOptions<MyOptions>` (or `IOptionsSnapshot` for scoped reloads) and read `.Value`.
4. Confirm the right appsettings.{Environment}.json is present and ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT is correct.

entries.title: SignalR negotiation/connection failed (CORS or transport)
entries.signature: SignalR Error during negotiation request failed WebSocket connection 404 hub CORS credentials
entries.cause: The SignalR client can't reach the hub negotiate endpoint, or CORS blocks the connection, or the hub route isn't mapped.
entries.solution:
1. Map the hub: `app.MapHub<ChatHub>("/chat")` and use the same URL on the client.
2. For cross-origin clients enable CORS with `.AllowCredentials()` and `.WithOrigins(...)` (not AllowAnyOrigin with credentials).
3. Ensure WebSockets are enabled on the host/proxy (IIS WebSocket feature, Azure WebSockets ON).
4. Confirm `UseRouting`/auth ordering allows the hub path.

entries.title: The antiforgery token could not be decrypted (Data Protection keys)
entries.signature: CryptographicException The key was not found in the key ring antiforgery data protection keys multiple servers
entries.cause: Data Protection keys aren't shared/persisted across instances or restarts (e.g. multiple servers, containers, or a fresh container filesystem), so tokens/cookies encrypted by one instance can't be read by another.
entries.solution:
1. Persist keys to a shared store: `AddDataProtection().PersistKeysToFileSystem(sharedDir)` or to Azure Blob/Redis.
2. In a web farm set a common application name with `SetApplicationName`.
3. In containers mount a persistent volume for the keys directory.

entries.title: 405 Method Not Allowed on an API endpoint
entries.signature: 405 Method Not Allowed HttpGet HttpPost attribute route verb mismatch
entries.cause: The request HTTP verb doesn't match the action's attribute (e.g. POSTing to a `[HttpGet]` action), or the route matches a different verb.
entries.solution:
1. Match the client's verb to the action attribute (`[HttpGet]`, `[HttpPost]`, etc.).
2. Ensure the route template is correct and not shadowed by another action.
3. For CORS preflight, allow the method in your CORS policy.

entries.title: CS0246: The type or namespace name could not be found
entries.signature: CS0246 The type or namespace name could not be found are you missing a using directive or an assembly reference
entries.cause: The compiler can't find a type — a missing `using`, a missing NuGet/project reference, or a target-framework mismatch between projects.
entries.solution:
1. Add the correct `using` namespace (IDE quick-fix often suggests it).
2. Add the NuGet package or project reference that defines the type.
3. Ensure referenced projects target a compatible framework.
4. Restore packages (`dotnet restore`) and rebuild.

entries.title: CS0103: The name does not exist in the current context
entries.signature: CS0103 The name does not exist in the current context variable scope misspelled
entries.cause: A referenced identifier isn't in scope — misspelled name, variable declared in another block, or a missing using for a static member.
entries.solution:
1. Check spelling and that the variable/member is declared and in scope.
2. For extension/static members add the right `using` (or `using static`).
3. Ensure the member's access modifier allows use from this location.

entries.title: NU1101: Unable to find package (NuGet restore)
entries.signature: NU1101 Unable to find package no packages exist source restore feed
entries.cause: NuGet can't find the package on any configured feed — wrong package id/version, a missing private feed, or offline.
entries.solution:
1. Verify the package id and version exist on nuget.org.
2. Add/restore the required feed in NuGet.config (private/Azure Artifacts) with credentials.
3. Run `dotnet restore` (or clear caches with `dotnet nuget locals all --clear`).
4. Check internet/proxy access to the feed.

entries.title: MSB3644: The reference assemblies for framework were not found
entries.signature: MSB3644 The reference assemblies for were not found targeting pack not installed
entries.cause: The targeting pack/SDK for the project's target framework isn't installed on the build machine.
entries.solution:
1. Install the matching .NET SDK / targeting pack for the TargetFramework.
2. Verify with `dotnet --list-sdks`.
3. Use a `global.json` to pin a known-installed SDK version.
4. On CI, add the setup-dotnet step for the required version.

entries.title: NETSDK1004: Assets file project.assets.json not found
entries.signature: NETSDK1004 Assets file project.assets.json not found run a restore
entries.cause: The project hasn't been restored, so the obj/project.assets.json file MSBuild needs doesn't exist.
entries.solution:
1. Run `dotnet restore` (or build, which restores by default).
2. If it persists, delete `bin`/`obj` and restore again.
3. On CI ensure a restore step runs before build/test.

entries.title: 404 Not Found for a route that should exist (routing/endpoint)
entries.signature: 404 Not Found route not matched MapControllers UseRouting endpoint missing attribute route
entries.cause: No endpoint matched the request — missing `MapControllers`/endpoint mapping, wrong route template, or middleware ordering that short-circuits routing.
entries.solution:
1. Ensure `app.MapControllers()` / `app.MapControllerRoute(...)` (or minimal API `app.MapGet(...)`) is present.
2. Verify the attribute route template and HTTP verb match the URL.
3. Keep ordering: `UseRouting` -> auth -> `UseEndpoints`/Map*.
4. Check for case/segment mismatches and required route values.

entries.title: InvalidOperationException: No service for type 'DbContext' has been registered
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException No service for type DbContext has been registered AddDbContext missing
entries.cause: A controller/service requests a DbContext that was never registered with the DI container.
entries.solution:
1. Register it in Program.cs: `builder.Services.AddDbContext<MyDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(connectionString));`.
2. Ensure the DbContext has a constructor accepting `DbContextOptions<MyDbContext>`.
3. Confirm the connection string exists in configuration.

entries.title: DbUpdateException / DbUpdateConcurrencyException on SaveChanges
entries.signature: DbUpdateException DbUpdateConcurrencyException SaveChanges inner SqlException constraint unique foreign key concurrency rowversion
entries.cause: SaveChanges failed at the database: a constraint violation (unique/foreign key/not-null) wraps the real error in InnerException, or a concurrency token (rowversion) didn't match for `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`.
entries.solution:
1. Read `ex.InnerException` for the actual SQL error (unique key, FK, NULL).
2. Fix the data or add the missing related row before saving.
3. For concurrency, catch `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`, reload entries, and re-apply changes.
4. Add a `[Timestamp]`/rowversion property if optimistic concurrency is intended.

entries.title: Localhost connection refused / app not reachable on expected port
entries.signature: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED localhost port wrong launchSettings ASPNETCORE_URLS not listening
entries.cause: The browser hits a port the app isn't listening on — mismatched launchSettings, container port not published, or the app bound to localhost only.
entries.solution:
1. Use the URL/port the app logs at startup ("Now listening on: ...").
2. Set `ASPNETCORE_URLS` (e.g. `http://0.0.0.0:5000`) to bind all interfaces.
3. In Docker publish the port (`-p 8080:8080`) and bind to 0.0.0.0.
4. Check launchSettings.json `applicationUrl` matches what you open.

entries.title: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT wrong / Development features in Production
entries.signature: environment Production Development appsettings not loaded developer exception page not showing ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
entries.cause: The hosting environment isn't set as expected, so the wrong appsettings.{Environment}.json loads and environment-gated features (developer exception page, Swagger) behave unexpectedly.
entries.solution:
1. Set `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` (launchSettings for local; app setting/env var on the server).
2. Verify with `app.Environment.EnvironmentName` or a log at startup.
3. Ensure appsettings.{Environment}.json exists and overrides correctly.
4. Don't rely on the developer exception page in Production; add proper exception handling.
